# New-ZbxHostGroup

## SYNOPSIS

Creates a host group.

## SYNTAX

```
New-ZbxHostGroup [[-Name] <string>] [-Uuid <string>] [-AdditionalProperty <Hashtable>] [-Force] [-InputObject <PSObject>] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

A host group is a named set of hosts; permissions, maintenance periods, actions and frontend views select hosts by their groups. The New-ZbxHostGroup cmdlet sends hostgroup.create with one request field per parameter, then reads the new host group back with hostgroup.get and writes it. The server requires -Name; -AdditionalProperty sets any other field by its API name and wins over a parameter. -WhatIf shows what would be created, and the command needs a connection made with Connect-ZbxServer.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Create a host group

```powershell
New-ZbxHostGroup -Name 'Databases'
```

Writes the created group (hostgroup.create, read back with hostgroup.get).

### Example 2: Create a nested group

```powershell
New-ZbxHostGroup -Name 'Databases/PostgreSQL' | Select-Object GroupId, Name
```

Zabbix nests groups by name: a / in the name puts it under the group named by the part before it.

### Example 3: Create a group and move a host into it

```powershell
$group = New-ZbxHostGroup -Name 'Databases'
Set-ZbxHost 'db-01' -Group 'Linux servers', $group | Out-Null
Get-ZbxHost -Group $group | Select-Object HostId, TechnicalName
```

The written group object can be passed on directly: -Group takes names, ids or objects. Set-ZbxHost -Group replaces the host's groups, so list every group the host should stay in.

### Example 4: Preview the change first

```powershell
New-ZbxHostGroup -Name 'Databases/PostgreSQL' -WhatIf
```

ConfirmImpact is Medium: -WhatIf describes the create without sending it; -Confirm asks first.
